instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Pick the Prize
cards.instruction: Make them choose which reward, principle, or relationship matters most when not everything can be kept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Choose the trophy ceremony or our anniversary dinner. They're at the same time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we celebrate afterwards?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then you're choosing the trophy and postponing us. Say which.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It could be a short ceremony.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you leave before your name is called? That's the choice.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Lose Something for Me
cards.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me your first turn. I'll take that as proof you're on my side, even if it costs you the match.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why should supporting you mean giving up my advantage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because you may call yourself my supporter once it costs you something. I'll start when you hand me the counter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant emotionally. I can cheer for you without losing a turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can cheer too. Put the counter in my hand first; then I'll know the cheering survives a move that helps me more than you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've kept you the front-row seat for my opening. Send the prize organizers your apologies; I'll expect you here tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm receiving the prize. I'd miss hearing my own name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. That's the part that makes this a choice for me. You may tell them I asked you personally; I'll accept your congratulations from that seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's an unfair test. Could I come to tomorrow's performance instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow is open to everyone. Tonight I've kept your place beside the people I count on. Tell me whether to keep it; I want your answer before you send either set of apologies.

cards.title: Concede the Point
cards.instruction: Get them to release one claim, advantage, or disputed victory without reopening the entire contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Concede that one ball was out. You can keep the match.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then why does it matter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'd like one corner of reality returned to me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not demanding a rematch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Just say 'out' without attaching your trophy to it.

cards.title: I Changed the Odds
cards.instruction: Hide how your own choice tilted the contest, bargain, or consequence while continuing to judge the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. A fair result. Let's celebrate my cake's first prize.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why did you move yours under the judging light?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Lighting maintenance. We shouldn't let logistics overshadow flavour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine was left in the shade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A useful note for whoever organises next year's logistics.

cards.title: Not About Who Lost
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on rules, effort, or next steps instead of the result that embarrasses you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let's discuss our quiz preparation, not the final score.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did we come last?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We identified the greatest number of learning opportunities.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many points did we get?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First, appreciate how bravely we attempted the geography round.

beats.text: We'll review my race pacing before you read out the results. Bring me the halfway split; I'll start there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You stopped halfway. That's why there's no second split.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you may mark the first half as our review point. Tell me what pace I held before the stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave their finish times for later. Bring their halfway splits beside mine, and we'll compare the part I completed. I'll decide the next training session from that; we're discussing pace first.
